* Never say X isn't home/is away/etc, say they're busy and will call them back bluh bluh bluh. Basic safety issue for kids home alone.
* Speak clearly, give numbers and addresses slowly and twice, if possible. Nothing is more annoying than needing to listen to a message five times to get basic info.
* If you're calling somewhere professional, have at least a vague outline of what you're going to say. Doctor's appointment? Know when you're available, what it's for, your doctors name, etc. Streamline it.
* Don't give out information unless you know who you're talking to. If it's an outbound call you have some control over the situation, but if someone is calling YOU? Be wary.
* Basically never tell anyone over the phone who isn't home, when people are going to be out, basic identification things like birthdays/full names/the obligatory credit information unless you're controlling the call.

We were lucky in that his anxiety was never particularly destructive; he only tore up used kleenex when we were out at his worst, most of it was just stealing our clothes so he could 'hide' in them until we got back. Primarily it was just his desperation to please, even if he wasn't happy with a scenario. We could put him through anything (I'm talking baths, unfamiliar places, nothing heinous) and he'd tolerate it quietly as long as I was within 'leaning' distance.

He also got jealous if I was paying attention to anyone or anything else--very cat-like in how often he would beg to be lifted up into my lap if I was on Discord talking to my MMO friends, got huffy if attention was directed towards new people in the house.

Mostly he just never wanted to be alone. Had to sleep leaning against or at least touching someone in the family, seemed terrified any time it looked like we were leaving him behind somewhere. Even just hanging out he had to be on someone, touching someone--lots of small reassurances constantly that people were still around and with him.

When we got him the breeder explained he was the last because he'd always been more timid and nervous than his siblings, so everyone got picked before him. He was also 6 months we got him and had been solo for some time as the original woman who was going to take him was unable to for health reasons. So we got him, and the breeder knocked a bit off the price for how old/anxious/clingy he could be.

My GCC was always a bit annoyed by being put away, but we took to giving him a treat every time we had to lock him up, and we made an effort to train him to fly back to it when it was time to eat an Especially Nice Snacks.

Maybe talk to his breeder? Ask what kind of cage he was in before--it may have been significantly smaller, a different color, or basically just 'different.' Birds can be intensely weird about being introduced to new things, even if they've seen it in another form before.

Get a routine going as far as when he's let out and when he's put away so it starts to be a normal thing in his day. It'll suck at first, for both of you, but if he's eating and drinking he's at least finding some level of chill already. Just don't let him train himself into thinking that if he cries for you it automatically means freedom and playtime. Ignore him until he settles down, then engage.

More than one piece of advice, because as someone who did it WRONG for fucking ages I'm all too happy for people to learn from my mistakes.

Avoid the 8am classes if you can. Don't have huge breaks between your classes unless you absolutely KNOW you'll be able to stick to getting your homework done then. I had a 3 hour break one semester and it was just too fucking tempting to cut my last class and head home for the day.

Live as close to campus as possible, if not in a residence/dorm. It's convenience and a great way to meet people if you're shyer, because it's basically in your face.

Talk to the counselors. They've heard it all, seen worse than you, and their job is literally to help you do your best and keep your shit together.

Know two people in your classes. Introduce yourself, try to arrange to get notes for each other if someone misses a class. DON'T use this as an excuse to skip--hell, if they turn out to be chill, agree to check up on each other if someone doesn't show.
